Principles

What we willnever do.

The rules we build by. They are the reason a partner can trust what Scout hands them.

Evidence before opinion

Scout never presents an unverified claim as fact. When it cannot find proof, it says so.

People make the call

Scout prepares the case. Your partners make the decision, and the record shows who decided what.

Model-agnostic

We use the best model for each step and can switch as models improve, without changing your workflow.

Your data stays yours

Your decks, notes and memos are never used to train any model, and each firm is kept separate.

What Ziro does

The sharpest analystin the room.

Built to do the work a great associate does on a deal, on every deal, without cutting corners.

Reads everything

Every slide, model, transcript and data room file, including the footnotes humans skip.

Checks everything

Each claim goes to independent sources before it earns a verdict.

Argues both sides

A bull agent and a bear agent build the strongest case each way, so you see the whole deal.

Cites every sentence

Every line Ziro writes links back to the page or source it came from.

Remembers your firm Roadmap

Ziro recalls what your team decided on similar deals, and why.

Knows its limits

When evidence is missing, Ziro says unverified. It never fills the gap with a guess.

The dialectic framework

Every deal arguedfrom both sides.

Ziro doesn't trust a single answer. It makes its agents disagree, then lets the evidence decide, so your IC sees the strongest case for and against before anyone votes.

Thesis · Bull agent

Builds the strongest case to invest: market, team, traction and why now, each point tied to a source.

Antithesis · Bear agent

Attacks the same deal: contradicted claims, missing data, competitors the deck leaves out.

Synthesis · Research agent

Weighs both sides against independent evidence and writes the verdict into a memo, with every line cited.

What Scout does

A research teamin one window.

Scout does the reading, checking and first drafting. Your team spends its time on judgment.

01 · Reads everything

Every page.
Every number.

Decks, data rooms, financial models and founder updates. Scout reads them all and keeps a pointer to the exact page behind every answer.

  • PDFs, slides, spreadsheets and notes
  • Tables and charts read as data, not pictures
  • Every answer links back to its page
02 · Checks the claims

Nothing taken
on trust.

Every claim is checked against company registries, press, industry data and public profiles, then graded so you know exactly what is proven.

  • Supported, Partial, Contradicted or Unverified
  • The source and the exact quote for each verdict
  • Gaps listed as questions for the founders
03 · Argues both sides

Bull. Bear.
Research.

Three agents take positions and challenge each other, so your partners see the strongest case for and against before the meeting.

  • The upside, argued with evidence
  • The risks nobody wants to say out loud
  • Open questions that would change the answer

Ledger · evidence graph

Every claim.Every source.

Ledger keeps every claim Scout extracts, the verdict it reached and the sources behind it, in one graph your whole team can trace.

Request accessTalk to Ziro
Four verdicts

Proof hasfour states.

A claim is never simply true or false. Ledger records how much of it the evidence actually supports.

Supported

Independent sources confirm the claim as stated.

Supported

Partial

Some of it holds up. Ledger shows which part, and which part does not.

Partial

Contradicted

Independent evidence says otherwise. You see the source and the quote.

Contradicted

Unverified

No independent source either way yet. It becomes a question for the founders.

Unverified
Audit trail

Who checked what,
and when.

Every verdict, edit and override is logged with the person, the time and the reason. When a partner asks why a number is in the memo, the answer is one click away.

  • Full history for every claim
  • Human overrides recorded with a reason
Missing information

Know what
you don't know.

Ledger lists the claims it could not confirm and turns them into specific questions, so your founder call goes straight to what matters.

  • Gaps ranked by how much they affect the decision
  • Questions written for the founder call
  • Answers flow back into the graph

Anatomy

Built the waypartners read.

Recommendation first, then the evidence, then the open questions. Your template, your sections.

Recommendation

A clear call with the three reasons behind it, written for a partner who has five minutes.

Claims and verdicts

Every key claim from the deck with its verdict and sources, ready to drill into.

Bull and bear

The strongest case for and against, argued from evidence rather than adjectives.

Market and competition

Market size rebuilt bottom-up, and the competitors the deck left out.

Open questions

What still needs proof, written as questions for the next founder call.

Citations everywhere

Hover any sentence to see its source. Click to open the page it came from.

Your format

Your template.
Your voice.

Memo follows a clear IC structure with every line cited. Learning your firm’s own format is on the roadmap. Partners get the document they are used to, only faster.

  • Firm templates and section order
  • Comments and edits tracked in Ledger

Vault · decision memory · roadmap

Rememberevery decision.

Vault keeps what you saw, what you decided and why. When a company you passed on raises again, you know exactly what changed.

Request accessSee the platform
Why it matters

Your firm’sreal moat.

Most funds lose the reasoning behind their decisions the day the meeting ends. Vault keeps it, and makes it searchable.

What you knew, when

Every decision is stored with the evidence that existed at the time, so you judge the call fairly later.

Revisit with context

When a passed company comes back, Vault shows the old concerns and checks which ones still hold.

Learn from outcomes

Track how decisions played out and spot patterns in what your firm gets right and wrong.

Portfolio monitoring

Claims don't stop
at the term sheet.

After you invest, Vault keeps checking. Founder updates are compared with the claims made at the time of the deal, and changes are flagged early.

  • Founder updates checked against earlier claims
  • Alerts when key numbers drift
  • One timeline per company

    DiligenceOct 2, 20266 min readZirnoro team

    Every pitch deck is a stack of claims

    A deck is a set of statements written to persuade. Treating each one as a claim to check changes how a fund reads it.

    A pitch deck is not a description of a company. It is an argument for one. Every slide is built to make the next meeting more likely, which is exactly what a founder should do. The problem starts when the reader treats it as a record.

    Read it as claims

    Take any seed deck and underline every statement that would change your decision if it were false. Market size. Number of paying customers. Growth rate. Gross margin. The team’s previous exits. Patents. Most decks carry fifteen to twenty-five of these.

    Each one can be checked, partly checked, or not checked at all yet. That is a much more useful way to read a deck than deciding whether you like it.

    The question is not whether the deck is convincing. It is how much of it is proven.

    What changes when you do this

    • Founder calls get sharper, because you arrive knowing what is unproven.
    • Partners compare deals on evidence rather than on how polished the deck looks.
    • Strong companies with plain decks stop getting overlooked.

    This is the idea Scout is built on. It reads the deck, lists the claims and checks each one against independent sources, then shows you what holds up. The judgment stays with you.

    Try it on a real deal

    Scout runs these checks on every deck you give it.

    ProductSep 26, 20265 min readZirnoro team

    Supported, partial, contradicted, unverified

    Why we grade claims on four levels instead of true or false, and what each one means for your decision.

    Early versions of Scout labelled claims true or false. It did not work. Real evidence is rarely that clean, and a binary label hides exactly the detail an investor needs.

    The four verdicts

    • Supported: independent sources confirm the claim as stated.
    • Partial: some of it holds. Two of three pilots are confirmed, for example.
    • Contradicted: independent evidence says otherwise, such as a competitor the deck says does not exist.
    • Unverified: nothing either way yet. This is not a red flag on its own, it is a question for the founders.
    Unverified is not the same as false. It is where the founder call should start.

    Every verdict comes with its sources and the exact quote behind it. If a partner disagrees, they can override it, and the override is logged with a reason.

    Why your IC memo should cite every line

    A memo without sources asks the committee to trust the writer. A cited memo lets them check.

    Investment memos are usually written under time pressure by the person most excited about the deal. That is not a criticism, it is how the process works. But it means the committee is often trusting the writer rather than the evidence.

    Citations change the conversation

    When every sentence links to its source, IC discussion moves from whether a number is right to what it means. Disagreements get settled by opening the source rather than by seniority.

    A cited memo turns an argument about facts into an argument about judgment.

    Memo writes this way by default. Each sentence is generated from verified claims, and hovering over it shows where it came from.

    Decision memory: the moat most funds throw away

    The reasoning behind a pass is worth as much as the reasoning behind an investment. Most firms lose both.

    Ask a fund why it passed on a company two years ago and you will usually get a vague answer. The partner who led the discussion may have left. The notes, if they exist, sit in someone’s inbox.

    Why it matters

    Companies come back. They raise the next round, pivot or get acquired. Without the original reasoning, a fund cannot tell whether its concerns were answered, and it cannot learn from the calls it got wrong.

    • Keep what you knew at the time of the decision, not just the decision.
    • Record the concerns that drove a pass, so they can be checked later.
    • Track outcomes so the firm learns which signals actually mattered.
    Institutional memory is the one advantage a fund builds that nobody else can copy.

    Vault exists to keep this record automatically, as a side effect of doing diligence in Zirnoro.

    Bull, Bear, Research: why we make agents argue

    One agent tends to agree with the deck. Three agents with opposing jobs find what it missed.

    Language models are agreeable. Give one a well-written deck and ask for an assessment, and it tends to repeat the deck’s framing. That is the opposite of what diligence needs.

    Three jobs, on purpose

    • The Bull agent makes the strongest case for the investment, using only verified evidence.
    • The Bear agent looks for every reason the deal could fail.
    • The Research agent settles factual disputes between them by finding sources.

    The result is not a verdict. It is a clear map of where the case is strong, where it is weak and which open question would change the answer.

    A practical diligence checklist for seed rounds

    The checks worth doing on every seed deal, and how long each one really takes.

    Seed diligence is a balance. Check too little and you miss obvious problems. Check too much and you lose the round. This is the list we see good investors run on almost every deal.

    The company

    • Confirm the legal entity, incorporation date and directors in the official company registry.
    • Check the cap table matches what the founders described.
    • Look for any existing liabilities or disputes on public record.

    The traction

    • Ask for evidence behind every paying customer named in the deck.
    • Separate signed contracts from pilots and letters of intent.
    • Ask for the raw numbers behind any growth rate.

    The market

    • Rebuild the market size bottom-up from customer count and price.
    • Search for competitors the deck leaves out.
    Most of this is reading and searching. That is the part software should do.

    Scout runs most of these checks automatically and lists the ones that need a person, such as a reference call.

    Legal

    Privacypolicy.

    Last updated October 9, 2026

    Who we areWhat we collectHow we use itNo training on your contentPublic sources and verificationWho we share data withHow long we keep itYour rightsSecurityChanges to this policy

    Who we are

    Zirnoro ("we", "us") builds VC Scout, an evidence-first investment research platform for venture funds, accelerators, incubators, angel networks and corporate venture teams, and Ziro, our investment intelligence agent. This policy covers both products. It explains what personal data we collect, why, and the choices you have. Questions can be sent to founder@zirnoro.in.

    What we collect

    • Account details: name, work email, firm, role and login information.
    • Customer content: pitch decks, data room files, notes, questions you ask Scout, and the claims, verdicts and memos Scout produces. These may contain personal data about founders and other people named in them.
    • Website and form data: what you submit through our access, partner and contact forms.
    • Usage data: basic logs such as pages visited, features used, device and browser type, used to run and improve the service.

    How we use it

    • To provide the service: reading documents, extracting and checking claims, and generating answers and memos for your firm.
    • To keep the service secure, including the audit trail of who did what.
    • To respond to requests and send service messages.
    • To improve the product using aggregated usage data that does not include your customer content.

    No training on your content

    We do not use customer content to train or fine-tune any AI model, and we only use AI model providers that contractually agree not to train on it. Your decks, notes and memos are processed only to deliver the service to your firm.

    Public sources and verification

    To check a claim, Scout searches public sources such as company registries, press and patent records. These searches use short queries about the claim and do not include your confidential documents. Results are shown to your firm only.

    Who we share data with

    We do not sell personal data. We share it only with service providers that help us run Zirnoro (such as cloud hosting and AI model providers), under contracts that limit their use of it, or when required by law. Each firm’s content is kept separate and is never shown to another firm.

    How long we keep it

    Customer content is kept for as long as your firm’s account is active, or until you delete it. Deleted content is removed from active systems promptly and from backups on a fixed schedule. Form submissions are kept as long as needed to respond and follow up.

    Your rights

    Depending on where you are, including under India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, you may have the right to access, correct or delete your personal data, to withdraw consent, and to raise a grievance. Email founder@zirnoro.in and we will respond within a reasonable time. People whose details appear in documents a customer uploads can also contact us, and we will work with that customer to handle the request.

    Security

    Our security design calls for encryption in transit and at rest, firm-level isolation, role-based access and audit logging. These are on our roadmap and have not yet been independently audited. No system is perfectly secure, and we will notify affected customers of a breach as required by law.

    Changes to this policy

    We will post updates here and change the date at the top. For material changes we will notify account holders before they take effect.

    Agreement

    These terms govern your use of the Zirnoro website and the Scout platform. By creating an account or using the service on behalf of a firm, you agree to them and confirm you are authorised to do so for that firm.

    The service

    Zirnoro provides AI-assisted research tools that read documents, extract claims, check them against public sources and draft memos. During the beta, features may change, and access is provided at our discretion.

    Not investment advice

    Scout supports research. It does not give investment, legal, tax or financial advice, and it does not make investment decisions. Verdicts and memos may be incomplete or wrong. Your firm remains fully responsible for its investment decisions and for checking information before relying on it.

    Your content

    You keep all rights to the documents and data you upload. You give us permission to process them only to provide the service to you. You confirm you have the right to upload them, including any obligations to the companies and people they describe.

    Acceptable use

    • Do not upload content you are not allowed to share.
    • Do not use the service to harass, defame or unlawfully profile any person.
    • Do not attempt to access another firm’s data or disrupt the service.
    • Do not reverse engineer or resell the service without our written permission.

    Confidentiality

    We treat your content as confidential and use it only to provide the service, as described in our privacy policy. We never use it to train AI models.

    Our intellectual property

    The Zirnoro platform, software, design and brand belong to us. Outputs Scout generates for you, such as memos, are yours to use within your firm.

    Fees

    Beta access may be free or discounted. Paid plans, if any, will be set out in a separate order form that takes priority over these terms where they differ.

    Limits of liability

    The service is provided as is during the beta. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for investment outcomes, and our total liability is limited to the fees you paid us in the twelve months before a claim.

    Ending the agreement

    You can stop using the service and ask us to delete your content at any time. We may suspend accounts that breach these terms. Sections on liability, intellectual property and confidentiality survive termination.

    Governing law

    These terms are governed by the laws of India. Disputes will be handled by the courts of Hyderabad, Telangana, unless a different arrangement is agreed in writing.

    Contact

    Questions about these terms can be sent to founder@zirnoro.in.
